Rafaella Tran (f), Indigo Tran (m); 4th; Stenwood Elementary School (FCPS in Dunn Loring) – Rising 5th
•	Both doing okay in school.
•	Took to Sylvan about a year ago for a year – concept of having tutoring was helpful for both kids
o	Was not happy with Sylvan’s approach at all 
	1. Customer service
	2. She will share other reason after we discuss our services

•	Rafaella
o	Has an IEP for reading, associating sounds with letters, encoding and decoding. 
	Been getting support in school and reading has improved significantly
	Also needs assistance in math – Did not pass math SOL
•	Tries her best every single time
•	Got same score for retake
o	Computer adaptive tests
o	Did take longer the second time – mom said to make sure she takes her time
o	I asked what she struggled with on the SOL and moms said she does not know all of the concepts
	IEP for math too, had for a couple of years now
	Vision and sight are fine
o	Has tremendous aptitude – second grade CogAT went very well – was very happy that I knew about the test and when it was administered. Sylvan team didn’t know anything about local schools ☹
o	Passed reading SOL and waiting for iReady scores – was below for fall and winter so not sure what will be.

•	Indigo 
o	Regularly scores high at school
o	Have been trying to get him into AAP but unsuccessfully.
o	In-place differentiated service in the classroom – not sufficient for him – just means that he gets harder worksheet than the other kids – still in 4th grade math
	They haven’t shared what keeping him out of AAP – reports that it’s out of school hands and in FCPS hands
	She has some significant concerns about the process
•	They say need to see examples of creative thinking rather than academics; e.g., turns over paper and draws map of Vienna, or pictures of dinosaurs
o	They are African American and need to live within the lines so won’t do that 
•	She finds the terms to get in suspect 
o	Do reading and math for him
	Every year gets selected for differentiated instruction and this year gets part-time one hour with gifted teacher a week
o	Very curious and do a lot of academics at home – this week she taught him exponents and square roots
o	Math is favorite subject
	Reading is not his go to, play soccer ball is choice, but can read well

o	Her daughter was bringing home 4’s but she couldn’t read.
o	School said they show effort versus academic achievement – what?!
o	She finds the report cards useless.

•	I asked about goals and gave some ideas:
o	Help Rafaella catch up where she needs it
o	Keep Indigo challenged and brain going – he rises to challenges
o	Reading and math both

•	Other significant issue – she shares custody with father; he doesn’t support any extra expense/activity for them
o	Only has them Wed during the SY
o	Then off and on over the summer and has the entire summer schedule in advance

•	Q’s
o	Is the work on computer or paper?
o	How measure success and how does she know about progress?
o	She is all for having them come for more than once/week during the school year, but due to custody arrangement, couldn’t be the same each week. Eg:
	Every WED she has them 
•	Had terrible attorneys for this arrangement
•	Then every other Wed through the next Mon.
o	So do waitlist for all other days but Wed during the school year?
•	Wants to show me the schedule to see what we could possibly make work. And to see our facility.
o	What is the product of our assessment?

•	Next Steps:
o	$150 assess – want to think about
o	$400-500/mo/kid 12 month
	Mid 50’s – low 60’s/hour
	60 day trial for refund
o	Sign up for assessments – see facility then
	50% assessment discount on website
o	Concerns of readout of the reports with each of them together – will do one at a time, then other do own thing
o	Assessments – 30min stagger start time

taken from 8/22 email:

My daughter, Elizabeth, just started her Third Grade year at Haycock Elementary.  She started school in APS (Glebe Elementary) in the 2019-2020 school year and suffered from missing most of kindergarten as Arlington didn't offer any virtual instruction after school shut down.  She started first grade at a DRA Level 2--a number of factors impacted her growth there (lack of kindergarten baseline, first time teacher, mostly virtual learning, etc.)  She was referred to a reading specialist, but with the virtual sessions I think she still struggled to get the help she really needed.  She caught up for the most part, but didn't finish at a 1st grade EOY benchmark.  

She worked with a specialist again last year and went to Sylvan two days a week.  She finished second grade at a DRA Level 28.  At the end of the year, her teacher reported that she was reading with 97% accuracy and at 82 words per minute.  She scored a 21/28 on reading comprehension, but struggles with phonics--short vowel sounds, final consonants (ck), digraphs (dge and tch), blends (scr an cr), and "magic e" words.  She needs practice on inflectional endings (s, ing, ed, and er) and on her overall writing.  She is reluctant to write completely, usually because it takes her longer than everyone else and she starts to rush.  She has great ideas, but struggles to get them down in a comprehensive way.

This year she has another first time teacher and while I am confident she'll progress, I would like to see if we can get her some independent tutoring.  She seemed to enjoy Sylvan, but it was all Computer Based work and I worry that she wasn't getting the individualized help that would really help her thrive.

I am interested in learning more about the options you provide and how you think you may be able to help her.

Thank you,
Leah Socha
703-969-5325

-originally wanted to go to a boarding school for HS
-started having seizures due to his medications, felt embarrassed/ had to sleep for a long time

-McLean HS has been very supportive

-tries to study, gets overwhelmed

-dad has tried to help with figuring out/ navigating schoology and other portals. Sounds like some of it might be related to not knowing how to navigate the portals. 
-when dad checks, he has tons of missing assignments 
-takes meds for anxiety/ depression as well as ADD/ADHD

-sometimes has trouble with focusing/ needs redirection
-or really tired due to sickness
-at a new school where he doesn't really know anyone

to Anne-Lucie, me

Hi Katherine,
Irene was born in Switzerland was educated in French and English schools in Kenya and Senegal. In MArch 2020 we moved back to the US. She is bilingual in French and English, and her Spanish is good and fluent but with lots of gaps as she was never formally schooled in it.

She was in ESOL briefly, and during COVID, I do not think her struggles are those of a person who cannot communicate in English at this stage. She faces similar difficulties in reading in French as well. Could we improve her confidence in reading? Certainly ! Does she need more readings at her level? Yes, we have not always gotten the right fit. Furthermore, she still needs to discover the type of reading that she likes (fiction, non-fiction, etc). She tends to like comic books but we have tried to move her more to books. She has read Harry Potter and now she is struggling a bit with Enola Holmes.

We have had no formal feedback from her English teacher. She has only had the new teacher for two and a half months. But she is struggling as she has gotten a C in her first report card. 

Would you please be able to explain the type of approach (group vs individual); setting (digital vs in person); frequency and cost.

Many thanks

Agustin

•	Super sweet sometimes comes home in tears. Relational. Very hilarious. Thinks stupid and says others say  he’s stupid.
•	I shared that would have to see how he does in our environment.

•	Finally had her tested.
